museumExhibits.searchText: quine: ontological commitment quine · on what there is what entities must exist for our best regimented theories to be true? quantification, variables, regimentation, and theoretical commitment ontological commitment is assessed through the quantified structure of a theory. regimentation can expose hidden commitments and compare alternative formulations. ontology is pursued alongside decisions about the best overall scientific theory. analytic traditions: logic, language, and analysis holism, naturalism, and ontology

museumExhibits.label: Quine: Word and Object
museumExhibits.searchText: quine: word and object quine · word and object could all observable linguistic behavior determine one uniquely correct translation? radical translation, stimulus meaning, indeterminacy, and reference behavioral evidence constrains translation without necessarily determining one uniquely correct manual. reference can vary across systematically equivalent schemes while observable predictions remain stable. translation depends on a network of sentences and practices rather than isolated word-object pairing. analytic traditions: logic, language, and analysis holism, naturalism, and ontology

museumExhibits.label: Quine: Naturalized Epistemology
museumExhibits.searchText: quine: naturalized epistemology quine · epistemology naturalized what becomes of epistemology when knowing is studied as a natural process within science? evidence, psychology, science from within, and normative pressure inquiry begins within an inherited scientific worldview rather than outside all assumptions. empirical study can illuminate the relation between sensory input and theoretical output. naturalism challenges first philosophy while leaving debate about epistemic normativity open. analytic traditions: logic, language, and analysis holism, naturalism, and ontology

museumExhibits.label: Carnap: The Principle of Tolerance
museumExhibits.searchText: carnap: the principle of tolerance carnap · logical syntax and frameworks must inquiry discover one uniquely correct logical language before it can begin? frameworks, formal choice, explication, and pragmatic comparison formal frameworks may be chosen and engineered for purposes rather than discovered as the sole language of reality. internal questions are answered using the rules of a framework; framework choice invites pragmatic assessment. explication replaces an imprecise concept with a clearer one suited to systematic inquiry. analytic traditions: logic, language, and analysis holism, naturalism, and ontology

museumExhibits.label: Anscombe: Intention and the Question “Why?”
museumExhibits.searchText: anscombe: intention and the question “why?” anscombe · intention when is the question “why?” asking for an agent’s reason rather than a cause or prediction? intentional action, reasons, descriptions, and practical knowledge one bodily movement can fall under several descriptions with different intentional status. reasons for action are not merely inner events that causally precede movement. the relevant “why?” can be refused, answered, or shown not to apply in distinctive ways. analytic traditions: logic, language, and analysis action, intention, and ordinary language

museumExhibits.label: Anscombe: Practical Knowledge in Action
museumExhibits.searchText: anscombe: practical knowledge in action anscombe · knowing without observation how can an agent know what they are intentionally doing without discovering it as a spectator? practical direction, bodily action, error, and knowledge without observation practical knowledge is exercised in directing action, not copied from a prior observed fact. an intentional action can be known under one description while its consequences remain unknown. error and failure do not convert every practical judgment into an observational hypothesis. analytic traditions: logic, language, and analysis action, intention, and ordinary language

museumExhibits.label: Anscombe: Modern Moral Philosophy
museumExhibits.searchText: anscombe: modern moral philosophy anscombe · modern moral philosophy can concepts of moral obligation remain intact after their original law-like framework is abandoned? obligation, virtue, action description, consequences, and moral psychology ethical theory depends on a clear account of action, intention, pleasure, desire, and practical reasoning. anscombe challenges theories that permit any act when aggregate consequences appear favorable. the essay helped renew anglophone interest in virtue while differing from many later virtue ethics. analytic traditions: logic, language, and analysis action, intention, and ordinary language

museumExhibits.label: Anscombe: Truman, Protest, and Moral Absolutes
museumExhibits.searchText: anscombe: truman, protest, and moral absolutes anscombe · mr truman’s degree can deliberately killing noncombatants become permissible because leaders expect a better outcome? civilian immunity, intention, public dissent, and institutional honor anscombe distinguishes intending civilian deaths from merely foreseeing harmful side effects. institutional honors can become occasions for philosophical and political dissent. her protest joins action description to an absolute prohibition on intentionally killing the innocent. analytic traditions: logic, language, and analysis action, intention, and ordinary language

museumExhibits.label: Anscombe: Causality and Determination
museumExhibits.searchText: anscombe: causality and determination anscombe · causality and determination does causation always require a universal law or deterministic necessity? observable causal concepts, necessity, indeterminism, and singular cases causation and determinism are distinct concepts; causal relations need not guarantee outcomes. singular causal knowledge may rely on perceivable processes rather than inferred universal laws. a richer causal vocabulary begins with verbs of production, prevention, contact, and change. analytic traditions: logic, language, and analysis action, intention, and ordinary language

museumExhibits.label: Political Philosophy: Authority and Legitimacy
museumExhibits.searchText: political philosophy: authority and legitimacy political philosophy · authority and legitimacy what turns the exercise of political power into a right to rule? power, justification, consent, obligation, and the standing to govern de facto power describes control, while legitimacy concerns a justified right to rule. political obligation asks whether and why citizens owe compliance to institutions or laws. consent, fairness, democracy, rights, and public justification support different accounts of legitimacy. political action, justice, and democratic reason political philosophy, authority, and public action

museumExhibits.label: Political Philosophy: Public Action and Civil Disobedience
museumExhibits.searchText: political philosophy: public action and civil disobedience political philosophy · public action and dissent when may citizens openly break a law in order to challenge injustice? public protest, conscience, nonviolence, persuasion, and democratic change civil disobedience communicates a political claim through a deliberate breach of law. publicity and willingness to accept legal consequences matter in some theories but not all. organized protest can challenge which voices, injuries, and reasons institutions recognize. political action, justice, and democratic reason political philosophy, authority, and public action

museumExhibits.label: Arendt: The Human Condition
museumExhibits.searchText: arendt: the human condition arendt · the human condition what becomes possible when people act and speak together in a shared world? labor, work, action, plurality, natality, and the public realm action depends on plurality: distinct people share a world without becoming interchangeable. natality names the human capacity to begin, initiate, and introduce something unforeseen. a durable public world gives words and deeds a space of appearance and remembrance. political action, justice, and democratic reason political philosophy, authority, and public action

museumExhibits.label: Arendt: Eichmann, Judgment, and Responsibility
museumExhibits.searchText: arendt: eichmann, judgment, and responsibility arendt · eichmann in jerusalem how can grave wrongdoing be carried out through ordinary habits of thoughtlessness? judgment, responsibility, bureaucracy, controversy, and the banality of evil thoughtlessness can coexist with calculated conduct and participation in enormous crimes. following orders or administrative routines does not erase personal responsibility and judgment. arendt’s account links political evil to institutions without reducing guilt to an impersonal system. political action, justice, and democratic reason political philosophy, authority, and public action

museumExhibits.label: Rawls: A Theory of Justice
museumExhibits.searchText: rawls: a theory of justice rawls · a theory of justice which principles should govern the basic institutions of a fair society? equal liberties, fair opportunity, distribution, and the basic structure justice primarily evaluates major institutions and how they distribute rights, duties, opportunities, and prospects. basic liberties have priority and cannot simply be traded away for aggregate welfare or economic growth. the difference principle tests inequalities by their effects on the expectations of the least advantaged. political action, justice, and democratic reason justice, distribution, rights, and the state

museumExhibits.label: Rawls: The Original Position
museumExhibits.searchText: rawls: the original position rawls · original position and veil of ignorance what principles would people choose if no one could tailor the rules to personal advantage? fair choice, the veil of ignorance, primary goods, and public principles the veil of ignorance blocks information that would enable bargaining from arbitrary social advantage. parties choose principles for institutions, not detailed policies for one known historical society. the construction models fairness through restrictions on reasons rather than predicting real voter behavior. political action, justice, and democratic reason justice, distribution, rights, and the state

museumExhibits.label: Nozick: Anarchy, State, and Utopia
museumExhibits.searchText: nozick: anarchy, state, and utopia nozick · anarchy, state, and utopia how much may a state do without violating the rights of individuals? rights, side constraints, the minimal state, entitlement, and voluntary association rights constrain permissible means rather than entering only as values to maximize. a minimal state may protect against force, theft, and fraud while avoiding broader paternalistic or redistributive aims. voluntary communities can embody diverse ideals within a common framework of rights. political action, justice, and democratic reason justice, distribution, rights, and the state

museumExhibits.label: Nozick: Entitlement and Rectification
museumExhibits.searchText: nozick: entitlement and rectification nozick · acquisition, transfer, and rectification is a distribution just because of its pattern, or because of the history that produced it? historical justice, holdings, voluntary transfer, past wrongs, and repair historical principles assess how holdings arose, not only the shape of the current distribution. justice in transfer depends on voluntary exchange from holdings that were themselves legitimately held. rectification must address the effects of past violations rather than treating the status quo as a clean starting point. political action, justice, and democratic reason justice, distribution, rights, and the state

museumExhibits.label: Nussbaum: The Capabilities Approach
museumExhibits.searchText: nussbaum: the capabilities approach nussbaum · central human capabilities what must people genuinely be able to do and to be in order to live with dignity? substantive freedom, dignity, thresholds, plural capabilities, and political duties capabilities are substantive opportunities, while functionings are the beings and doings people actually realize. human dignity requires attention to several irreducible dimensions rather than one aggregate welfare measure. a threshold aims to secure each person’s minimum entitlement without ranking lives by productivity. political action, justice, and democratic reason capabilities, dignity, democracy, and public reason

museumExhibits.label: Nussbaum: Frontiers of Justice
museumExhibits.searchText: nussbaum: frontiers of justice nussbaum · frontiers of justice how should a theory of justice include people whose lives do not fit an ideal of independent cooperation? disability, dependency, care, nationality, species, and equal dignity dependency and care are normal features of human life rather than marginal exceptions to citizenship. justice should secure capabilities directly instead of treating productive reciprocity as the basis of equal worth. institutional inclusion requires material access, social recognition, support, and political voice together. political action, justice, and democratic reason capabilities, dignity, democracy, and public reason

museumExhibits.label: Amartya Sen: Capability and Development
museumExhibits.searchText: amartya sen: capability and development amartya sen · capability and development should development be measured by resources and growth, or by the freedoms people can actually exercise? functionings, agency, public reasoning, poverty, and human development functionings are achieved states and activities; capabilities are the real opportunities to select among them. agency includes a person’s ability to pursue goals they have reason to value, not only personal well-being. public reasoning helps communities identify valuable capabilities and scrutinize unequal freedom. political action, justice, and democratic reason capabilities, dignity, democracy, and public reason

museumExhibits.label: Habermas: The Public Sphere
museumExhibits.searchText: habermas: the public sphere habermas · the public sphere which social spaces allow public opinion to test power through reasons? communication, media, civil society, access, publicity, and democratic legitimacy a public sphere links civil society to political decision through communication and criticism. publicity can expose power to scrutiny, but media ownership and unequal access shape whose reasons circulate. democratic legitimacy depends on opinion and will formation beyond periodic voting alone. political action, justice, and democratic reason capabilities, dignity, democracy, and public reason

museumExhibits.label: Democratic Deliberation: Assembly and Public Reason
museumExhibits.searchText: democratic deliberation: assembly and public reason democracy · deliberation and assembly how can collective decisions be shaped by reasons people can exchange and contest? participation, equality, agenda setting, public reasons, voting, and institutional design deliberation asks participants to justify proposals with reasons others can examine and answer. political equality concerns access, voice, agenda-setting power, information, and uptake—not only a formal vote. voting can close a decision while public reasoning shapes preferences, alternatives, and future accountability. political action, justice, and democratic reason capabilities, dignity, democracy, and public reason

museumExhibits.label: Indian Philosophy: A Compendium Is Not the Whole Field
museumExhibits.searchText: indian philosophy: a compendium is not the whole field orientation · sarva-darśana-saṃgraha what becomes visible—or disappears—when one text arranges rival schools? a historically situated survey, not a neutral table of every tradition compendia preserve arguments while also ranking and framing them. a named school can contain centuries of disagreement and commentary. buddhist, materialist, devotional, regional, and vernacular traditions require routes beyond this hall. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems many schools, shared questions, and missing traditions

museumExhibits.label: Indian Philosophy: Texts Live in Manuscript Worlds
museumExhibits.searchText: indian philosophy: texts live in manuscript worlds orientation · text, script, and transmission how do philosophical texts travel through scripts, institutions, and practices? palm leaf, commentary, recitation, copying, and regional transmission composition date and manuscript date are different claims. sanskrit texts circulated in multiple regional scripts. commentary and institutional practice help constitute a text’s philosophical afterlife. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems many schools, shared questions, and missing traditions

museumExhibits.label: Mahāvīra: The Kalpa-sūtra Transmission
museumExhibits.searchText: mahāvīra: the kalpa-sūtra transmission mahāvīra · life, lineage, and memory how does a later manuscript shape the remembered life of a jina? birth narrative, festival recitation, lineage, and visual memory mahāvīra is situated within a prior tīrthaṅkara lineage. biography is transmitted through ritual, text, image, and commentary. later manuscripts are evidence for reception, not eyewitness records. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems jain worlds: soul, karma, nonviolence, and knowing

museumExhibits.label: Kaṇāda: Atoms, Dyads, and Composite Bodies
museumExhibits.searchText: kaṇāda: atoms, dyads, and composite bodies kaṇāda · vaiśeṣika atomism how can imperceptible atoms produce perceptible composite things? paramāṇu, combination, motion, difference, and material change atoms are enduring and imperceptible; composites arise through combination. kinds of atom help explain qualitative differences among material elements. motion, conjunction, disjunction, and causation are part of the account—not decorative additions. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems categories, atoms, and realist debate

museumExhibits.label: Kaṇāda’s Tradition: Perception and Inference
museumExhibits.searchText: kaṇāda’s tradition: perception and inference kaṇāda · vaiśeṣika epistemology how can an atomist and realist system justify claims about what cannot be perceived? perception, inference, testimony, and changing school boundaries perception concerns direct cognition under specified conditions. inference extends knowledge beyond what is immediately perceived. school lists of pramāṇas changed as traditions debated and merged. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems categories, atoms, and realist debate

museumExhibits.label: Patañjali: The Yoga Sūtra Manuscript Tradition
museumExhibits.searchText: patañjali: the yoga sūtra manuscript tradition patañjali · yoga sūtra transmission what can a late manuscript witness tell us about a much older and disputed textual lineage? aphorism, commentary, copying, authorship, and uncertain chronology the yoga sūtras organize practice, affliction, concentration, cognition, and liberation. aphoristic text and commentary are historically intertwined. recent integrated-text scholarship often places the pātañjalayogaśāstra around the fourth century ce, while earlier proposals remain debated. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems yoga, mind, discipline, and liberation

museumExhibits.label: Patañjali’s Yoga: Three Means of Knowledge
museumExhibits.searchText: patañjali’s yoga: three means of knowledge patañjali · cognition and error how does yoga distinguish reliable cognition from error and mental construction? perception, inference, testimony, and the disciplined analysis of mind valid cognition is one category within a wider analysis of mental fluctuations. perception, inference, and reliable testimony have different warrants. yoga shares concepts with sāṃkhya while developing a distinct practical and theological profile. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems yoga, mind, discipline, and liberation

museumExhibits.label: Śaṅkara: Commentary on the Aitareya Upaniṣad
museumExhibits.searchText: śaṅkara: commentary on the aitareya upaniṣad śaṅkara · bhāṣya and interpretation how does commentary turn inherited sentences into a systematic nondual argument? textual reconciliation, self-knowledge, superimposition, and liberation bhāṣya is sustained philosophical argument, not a neutral paraphrase. advaita distinguishes ultimate reality from ordinary empirical experience. liberation depends on knowledge, while discipline and inquiry prepare the knower. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems vedānta: rival readings of self, world, and brahman

museumExhibits.label: Madhva: Udupi and the Institutional Life of Dvaita
museumExhibits.searchText: madhva: udupi and the institutional life of dvaita madhva · school, practice, and institution how does a philosophical school persist through institutions, ritual, teaching, and succession? dvaita interpretation beyond a single author or proposition difference is real rather than a provisional appearance to be overcome. dependence on viṣṇu does not erase the individuality of selves or the reality of the world. institutions carry arguments through teaching, ritual, authority, and debate. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems vedānta: rival readings of self, world, and brahman

museumExhibits.label: Indian Philosophy: Many Traditions, One Deliberative Room
museumExhibits.searchText: indian philosophy: many traditions, one deliberative room indian philosophy · plurality and encounter what changes when disagreement is staged as an encounter rather than a list? a later mughal image of religious conversation, used with strict historical limits plurality includes real disagreement, not interchangeable wisdom. institutions and patrons shape which conversations become visible. a later image can illuminate reception without documenting an earlier debate. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems many schools, shared questions, and missing traditions

museumExhibits.label: Indian Philosophy: Nālandā and Knowledge as an Institution
museumExhibits.searchText: indian philosophy: nālandā and knowledge as an institution indian philosophy · institutions and travel what material and institutional conditions let arguments travel? teachers, students, libraries, patronage, commentary, and debate institutions preserve and reorganize philosophical work. travel brings arguments into new linguistic and political settings. material ruins do not transparently reconstruct classroom life. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems many schools, shared questions, and missing traditions

museumExhibits.label: Indian Philosophy: Aśoka’s Lion Capital and Public Dhamma
museumExhibits.searchText: indian philosophy: aśoka’s lion capital and public dhamma indian philosophy · ethics in public how does ethical language change when authority makes it public? imperial communication, moral vocabulary, religious plurality, and political power ethical vocabulary can travel through political institutions. public moral communication joins persuasion to authority. dhamma in aśokan usage should not be reduced to one later doctrine. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems many schools, shared questions, and missing traditions

museumExhibits.label: Jain Philosophy: Jambūdvīpa as Moral Geography
museumExhibits.searchText: jain philosophy: jambūdvīpa as moral geography jain philosophy · cosmos and condition how can a map locate beings within a morally structured cosmos? regions, cycles, embodied conditions, and the scale of liberation cosmology locates ethical and embodied possibilities. a diagram can organize scale without functioning as modern cartography. different jain cosmological images emphasize different structures. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems jain worlds: soul, karma, nonviolence, and knowing

museumExhibits.label: Jain Philosophy: Samavasaraṇa and the Open Assembly
museumExhibits.searchText: jain philosophy: samavasaraṇa and the open assembly jain philosophy · teaching and nonviolence what would teaching look like if no kind of being were excluded? the jina’s teaching assembly, many audiences, order, and peaceful attention the assembly joins omniscient teaching to universal accessibility. nonviolence governs relations among radically different beings. ordered visual form carries doctrinal and devotional meaning. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems jain worlds: soul, karma, nonviolence, and knowing

museumExhibits.label: Jain Philosophy: The Tīrthaṅkara’s Stillness
museumExhibits.searchText: jain philosophy: the tīrthaṅkara’s stillness jain philosophy · renunciation and liberation how can an image make disciplined detachment visible? stillness, restraint, the liberated teacher, and the limits of portraiture a jina is a victor over bondage, not a creator deity. stillness can signify disciplined freedom from attachment. iconographic identity differs from historical portrait likeness. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems jain worlds: soul, karma, nonviolence, and knowing

museumExhibits.label: Kaṇāda’s Realist Context: Argument Before Authority
museumExhibits.searchText: kaṇāda’s realist context: argument before authority nyāya–vaiśeṣika · public argument what makes a reason answerable to an opponent? claim, reason, challenge, response, and the discipline of disagreement argument exposes a claim to structured challenge. reasons depend on shared standards and disputed examples. a proxy image must never be relabeled as historical documentation. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems categories, atoms, and realist debate

museumExhibits.label: Kaṇāda’s Intellectual World: The Spitzer Manuscript Fragments
museumExhibits.searchText: kaṇāda’s intellectual world: the spitzer manuscript fragments sanskrit philosophy · early material witness what can a damaged manuscript reveal about an argumentative world? fragments, classification, debate, silk road transmission, and cautious reconstruction fragmentary evidence can still reveal structures of argument. sanskrit philosophical texts traveled across long-distance networks. a material witness should not be assigned to a school without evidence. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems categories, atoms, and realist debate

museumExhibits.label: Kaṇāda’s Realist Context: Smoke, Fire, and Inference
museumExhibits.searchText: kaṇāda’s realist context: smoke, fire, and inference nyāya–vaiśeṣika · inference when does smoke justify an inference to fire? observed sign, pervasion, background conditions, and possible defeaters inference moves from a recognized sign to an unobserved target. the sign-target relation requires more than one coincidental pairing. context and defeaters determine whether the reasoning succeeds. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems categories, atoms, and realist debate

museumExhibits.label: Patañjali’s Yoga in Reception: Six Yogis Under a Banyan
museumExhibits.searchText: patañjali’s yoga in reception: six yogis under a banyan yoga · practice and community what becomes visible when yoga is shown as shared discipline? posture, attention, instruction, community, and a much later visual tradition practice is transmitted through people and settings as well as texts. shared discipline can coexist with inward concentration. later yogic imagery cannot be assigned automatically to pātañjala yoga. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems yoga, mind, discipline, and liberation

museumExhibits.label: Patañjali’s Yoga in Context: Posture, Restraint, and Inner Heat
museumExhibits.searchText: patañjali’s yoga in context: posture, restraint, and inner heat yoga · embodied discipline how can posture become part of a disciplined transformation? a crossed posture, meditation strap, ascetic heat, and the danger of false attribution posture supports sustained attention rather than functioning as display alone. ascetic heat links disciplined effort with transformation. shared practices do not erase doctrinal and institutional difference. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems yoga, mind, discipline, and liberation

museumExhibits.label: Patañjali’s Yoga in Reception: The Ascetic Princess Āsāvarī
museumExhibits.searchText: patañjali’s yoga in reception: the ascetic princess āsāvarī yoga · gender, asceticism, and reception who disappears when ascetic practice is pictured only through male sages? a female ascetic personification, wilderness, music, and careful comparison visual canons shape who appears to count as a practitioner. ragamala painting joins music, mood, poetry, and personification. a contextual comparison must preserve the work’s actual genre. classical south asia: jain, yoga, and brahmanical systems yoga, mind, discipline, and liberation

museumExhibits.label: The Buddha’s Teachings: Early Discourses in Transmission
museumExhibits.searchText: the buddha’s teachings: early discourses in transmission early buddhist texts · communal memory how do teachings associated with an oral community become surviving texts? recitation, collection, variation, copying, and material fragility oral and textual transmission are historical processes. different canons preserve overlapping and divergent collections. a surviving manuscript date is not the date of the teaching it carries. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge many buddhist paths and early discourses

museumExhibits.label: Nāgārjuna’s Context: Prajñāpāramitā in Manuscript
museumExhibits.searchText: nāgārjuna’s context: prajñāpāramitā in manuscript madhyamaka context · perfection of wisdom how did emptiness arguments develop alongside the perfection of wisdom literature? wisdom, non-grasping, bodhisattva practice, and later tibetan transmission emptiness is joined to practice rather than offered as a detached theory. madhyamaka and prajñāpāramitā are related but not identical. later tibetan manuscripts witness reception, not nāgārjuna’s authorship. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge madhyamaka: emptiness and dependence

museumExhibits.label: Nāgārjuna: Dependent Arising and Emptiness
museumExhibits.searchText: nāgārjuna: dependent arising and emptiness nāgārjuna · dependence without essence why does dependence undermine independent essence rather than ordinary causal life? conditioned arising, conventional truth, emptiness, and the rejection of nihilism dependent things are empty of independent essence. conventional relations remain indispensable. emptiness itself must not be reified into a hidden substance. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge madhyamaka: emptiness and dependence

museumExhibits.label: Vasubandhu’s Abhidharmakośa: Analysis and Critique
museumExhibits.searchText: vasubandhu’s abhidharmakośa: analysis and critique vasubandhu · treasury of abhidharma how can experience be analyzed without positing a permanent self? dharmas, causation, cognition, karma, and vasubandhu’s critical commentary analysis breaks the person into conditioned processes without denying continuity. the commentary records argument within buddhist scholasticism. vasubandhu’s intellectual biography and affiliations remain debated. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge abhidharma to yogacara

museumExhibits.label: Vasubandhu’s Mere Ideation: Representation and Experience
museumExhibits.searchText: vasubandhu’s mere ideation: representation and experience vasubandhu · vijñaptimātratā what changes when experience is analyzed through representation rather than external objects as ordinarily assumed? cognition, appearance, karmic continuity, and rival readings of yogācāra experience is examined through representational and causal processes. the ordinary subject-object split is not taken for granted. modern labels such as “idealism” remain interpretive and contested. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge abhidharma to yogacara

museumExhibits.label: Xuanzang: Translation as Philosophical Labor
museumExhibits.searchText: xuanzang: translation as philosophical labor translation · travel · terminology what philosophical work occurs when texts cross languages and institutions? terminology, travel, commentary, institutions, and east asian yogācāra translation selects philosophical equivalents and creates new vocabularies. travel and institutions affect which texts become authoritative. east asian yogācāra develops rather than merely copies south asian debates. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge translation and transformation across asia

museumExhibits.label: Tibetan Manuscript Worlds: Text, Image, and Institution
museumExhibits.searchText: tibetan manuscript worlds: text, image, and institution transmission · manuscript culture how do translated texts acquire material, ritual, and institutional lives? pecha format, painting, recitation, commentary, collection, and use texts persist through skilled material and institutional practices. image and ornament can mark value without summarizing doctrine. tibetan philosophical traditions developed extensive new debates and curricula. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge translation and transformation across asia

museumExhibits.label: The Diamond Sūtra: Translation, Printing, and Circulation
museumExhibits.searchText: the diamond sūtra: translation, printing, and circulation east asia · print · public transmission how does printing change the scale and setting of buddhist textual life? chinese translation, patronage, image, text, reproducibility, and dunhuang printing changes reproducibility without fixing interpretation. translation and patronage shape which texts circulate. material history belongs inside philosophical history. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge translation and transformation across asia

museumExhibits.label: The Buddha’s First Sermon: Four Truths and a Path
museumExhibits.searchText: the buddha’s first sermon: four truths and a path buddha · four truths and the path how does diagnosis become a practical path out of suffering? suffering, its arising, its cessation, and disciplined cultivation the truths organize diagnosis, cause, possibility, and practice. the path joins ethical conduct, meditation, and understanding. later reliefs make communal memory visible without documenting the event. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge many buddhist paths and early discourses

museumExhibits.label: Buddhist Philosophy in Public: Aśoka’s Dhamma
museumExhibits.searchText: buddhist philosophy in public: aśoka’s dhamma early buddhism · ethics and empire what happens when ethical language enters imperial policy? public exhortation, religious patronage, welfare, authority, and political power patronage helped buddhist communities and monuments expand. public ethics can persuade while also expressing authority. aśokan dhamma is broader than a summary of buddhist doctrine. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge many buddhist paths and early discourses

museumExhibits.label: Buddhist Philosophy at Sanchi: Relics, Memory, and Saṅgha
museumExhibits.searchText: buddhist philosophy at sanchi: relics, memory, and saṅgha early buddhism · community and memory how do communities make teachings durable beyond a teacher’s life? relics, pilgrimage, donation, narrative, architecture, and communal practice communal practices transmit teachings alongside texts. architecture directs movement, attention, and memory. a monument accumulates historical layers and later interpretations. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge many buddhist paths and early discourses

museumExhibits.label: Nāgārjuna’s Root Verses: Arguments without Foundations
museumExhibits.searchText: nāgārjuna’s root verses: arguments without foundations nāgārjuna · mūlamadhyamakakārikā what remains when supposedly self-grounding things are analyzed? conditions, conceptual dependence, reductio arguments, and the middle way reductio arguments expose problems in claims of independent essence. dependent arising and emptiness illuminate one another. the middle way avoids both reified existence and simple annihilation. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge madhyamaka: emptiness and dependence

museumExhibits.label: Nāgārjuna and Āryadeva: Building a Madhyamaka Lineage
museumExhibits.searchText: nāgārjuna and āryadeva: building a madhyamaka lineage madhyamaka · teaching and development how does an argument become a lineage rather than remain one author’s work? teacher, student, commentary, debate, attribution, and later tibetan memory āryadeva extends and redirects madhyamaka argument. lineages preserve texts while also interpreting their relations. later images reveal reception, not historical appearance. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge madhyamaka: emptiness and dependence

museumExhibits.label: Nāgārjuna’s Context: Prajñāpāramitā, Wisdom beyond Reification
museumExhibits.searchText: nāgārjuna’s context: prajñāpāramitā, wisdom beyond reification madhyamaka · perfection of wisdom how can wisdom be personified without becoming a permanent essence? wisdom literature, emptiness, devotion, image, and later material reception prajñāpāramitā literature critiques attachment to fixed categories. personification can support devotion without asserting an eternal substance. madhyamaka and wisdom literature have related but complex histories. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge madhyamaka: emptiness and dependence

museumExhibits.label: Vasubandhu and Asaṅga: Building Yogācāra
museumExhibits.searchText: vasubandhu and asaṅga: building yogācāra vasubandhu · yogācāra development how does collaboration reshape an inherited analysis of mind? brothers in later memory, texts, attribution, practice, and contested intellectual development yogācāra developed through a corpus rather than one isolated doctrine. cognition is analyzed for soteriological transformation as well as theory. biographical and attribution questions remain open. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge abhidharma to yogacara

museumExhibits.label: Vasubandhu’s Abhidharma Context: A Structured Cosmos
museumExhibits.searchText: vasubandhu’s abhidharma context: a structured cosmos abhidharma · mount meru cosmology why would analysis of experience include a detailed cosmos? world systems, realms, karmic conditions, classification, and later visual transmission abhidharma classification joins psychology, cosmology, and causation. cosmic realms locate kinds of embodied and karmic condition. later visual traditions reorganize inherited models. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge abhidharma to yogacara

museumExhibits.label: Vasubandhu’s Yogācāra Lineage: Asaṅga across Asia
museumExhibits.searchText: vasubandhu’s yogācāra lineage: asaṅga across asia yogācāra · east asian reception how does an indian scholastic become present in a later east asian institution? hossō reception, portrait sculpture, lineage, translation, and historical distance east asian yogācāra developed through translation and commentary. portrait sculpture can materialize lineage authority. reception creates new intellectual forms rather than merely copying an origin. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge abhidharma to yogacara

museumExhibits.label: Buddhist Epistemology: Perception and Inference
museumExhibits.searchText: buddhist epistemology: perception and inference buddhist pramāṇa · knowledge sources why recognize perception and inference as distinct sources of knowledge? direct awareness, conceptual construction, reasons, error, and competing indian systems perception and inference have different objects and structures. concepts organize experience without simply copying unique particulars. reliability is tied to successful cognition and causal conditions. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge pramāṇa, perception, inference, and language

museumExhibits.label: Dignāga’s Scholastic World: Nālandā as Philosophical Practice
museumExhibits.searchText: dignāga’s scholastic world: nālandā as philosophical practice buddhist pramāṇa · institutions of debate what institutions turn reasoning into a durable practice? teaching, debate, commentary, travel, manuscripts, and the limits of archaeological inference arguments persist through institutions and trained communities. debate and commentary are social practices with material supports. archaeology cannot assign a surviving wall to a named philosopher without evidence. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge pramāṇa, perception, inference, and language

museumExhibits.label: Dharmakīrti’s Pramāṇavārttika: A Tradition of Commentary
museumExhibits.searchText: dharmakīrti’s pramāṇavārttika: a tradition of commentary dharmakīrti · reason and commentary how does a difficult work remain alive through commentary? inference, perception, authority, later portraiture, and a long tibetan curriculum the pramāṇavārttika became a central, contested commentarial work. reasoning and buddhist soteriology remain connected. later portrait conventions establish identity without preserving appearance. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge pramāṇa, perception, inference, and language

museumExhibits.label: Buddhist Transmission: Kumārajīva Translates the Middle Way
museumExhibits.searchText: buddhist transmission: kumārajīva translates the middle way translation · madhyamaka in chinese what philosophical choices occur inside translation? teams, terminology, textual selection, chinese madhyamaka, and a modern commemorative image translation creates and stabilizes philosophical vocabulary. text selection influences which arguments become canonical. chinese madhyamaka develops through interpretation, not passive copying. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge translation and transformation across asia

museumExhibits.label: Buddhist Transmission: Tripiṭaka Koreana, Canon and Carving
museumExhibits.searchText: buddhist transmission: tripiṭaka koreana, canon and carving korea · canon and woodblock printing what does it take to preserve a canon at enormous scale? carving, collation, storage, patronage, reproducibility, and korean buddhist history a canon is produced through selection, comparison, and material labor. woodblocks enable reproducibility while requiring exacting care. korean buddhist institutions actively shaped transmission. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge translation and transformation across asia

museumExhibits.label: Buddhist Transmission: Pāli Kammavācā in Southeast Asia
museumExhibits.searchText: buddhist transmission: pāli kammavācā in southeast asia southeast asia · discipline and material form how does disciplinary text become a distinctive ceremonial object? pāli recitation, monastic procedure, gilded leaves, local craft, and institutional continuity monastic discipline is enacted through communal procedures. material form can mark authority and ceremonial value. pāli transmission developed through distinctive regional practices. buddhist philosophies of liberation and knowledge translation and transformation across asia

museumExhibits.label: Warring States: Courts, Conflict, and Traveling Persuaders
museumExhibits.searchText: warring states: courts, conflict, and traveling persuaders warring states · political and intellectual geography how does competition among states change what philosophers are asked to do? courts, war, office, patronage, persuasion, mobility, and practical advice political fragmentation created both danger and opportunities for mobile specialists. arguments about virtue, standards, names, and power addressed institutional choices. no single “hundred schools” chart captures the overlap and later classification of texts. warring states & classical chinese traditions many ways in early china

museumExhibits.label: Excavated Bamboo Texts: Philosophy Before Fixed Canons
museumExhibits.searchText: excavated bamboo texts: philosophy before fixed canons manuscript culture · excavation and transmission what changes when an excavated witness differs from the book later generations received? manuscript layers, sequence, lost texts, variant wording, and editorial caution a received canon is the result of transmission, selection, loss, and editing. excavated manuscripts can reveal plurality without automatically replacing later texts. physical sequence and archaeological context are part of philosophical evidence. warring states & classical chinese traditions many ways in early china

museumExhibits.label: Gongsun Long and the School of Names: Is a White Horse a Horse?
museumExhibits.searchText: gongsun long and the school of names: is a white horse a horse? names and distinctions · white horse dialogue when does a more specific name change what can be admitted or selected? names, kinds, qualification, reference, disputation, and translation a general term and a qualified term can guide different acts of selection. the dialogue tests how names relate to kinds, properties, and admissible objects. its form stages disagreement rather than delivering an uncontested theory. warring states & classical chinese traditions many ways in early china

museumExhibits.label: Sunzi and Strategic Reason: Calculation Under Conflict
museumExhibits.searchText: sunzi and strategic reason: calculation under conflict strategy · information, position, and cost what kind of reasoning is possible when information is partial and the other side adapts? assessment, deception, position, timing, intelligence, cost, and uncertainty good strategy responds to conditions instead of repeating a fixed recipe. information and misdirection shape what each side believes is possible. winning at lower cost can be strategically rational without being ethically sufficient. warring states & classical chinese traditions many ways in early china

museumExhibits.label: The Analects: A Layered Record of Teaching and Reception
museumExhibits.searchText: the analects: a layered record of teaching and reception confucius · analects and transmission how can a layered collection preserve a teacher’s importance without becoming a transcript? sayings, disciples, compilation, ritual, humaneness, learning, and commentary the analects joins moral cultivation to relationships, ritual practice, and learning. its short units invite interpretation through placement, repetition, and commentary. confucius’s voice reaches readers through compilation rather than direct authorship. warring states & classical chinese traditions ritual, humaneness, cultivation, and human nature

museumExhibits.label: The Guodian Laozi: A Text Before a Fixed Daodejing
museumExhibits.searchText: the guodian laozi: a text before a fixed daodejing daodejing · early manuscript plurality what happens to authorship when early witnesses preserve only selected and differently ordered passages? textual strata, selection, sequence, titles, attribution, and the limits of a founder story early witnesses complicate the idea of one fixed daodejing from the start. attribution can organize a tradition even when a biography remains legendary or composite. variant order changes how adjacent passages appear to support one another. warring states & classical chinese traditions daodejing, zhuangzi, and the way

museumExhibits.label: Writing on Bamboo: Argument as Material Practice
museumExhibits.searchText: writing on bamboo: argument as material practice textual culture · bamboo, ink, and order how does a philosophical argument depend on the material form that carries it? cutting, smoothing, binding, inscribing, reordering, and preserving a text textual order was a material achievement rather than an invisible given. copying and compilation help explain why early works can contain layers and tensions. excavated witnesses can challenge assumptions created by later received editions. warring states & classical chinese traditions many ways in early china

museumExhibits.label: Confucian Ritual and Music: Formation Through Coordinated Practice
museumExhibits.searchText: confucian ritual and music: formation through coordinated practice confucian traditions · ritual and music how can patterned performance cultivate judgment, feeling, and relationship? timing, attention, role, emotion, coordination, and political order ritual cultivation works through embodied repetition, timing, and social coordination. music can order emotion without treating feeling as an enemy of reason. good form requires humane purpose; performance alone does not guarantee virtue. warring states & classical chinese traditions ritual, humaneness, cultivation, and human nature

museumExhibits.label: Zhuangzi’s Butterfly Dream: Perspective and Transformation
museumExhibits.searchText: zhuangzi’s butterfly dream: perspective and transformation zhuangzi · dream, waking, and transformation what makes one perspective the final measure of another? dreaming, waking, identity, transformation, and the limits of certainty the passage questions confidence in a single fixed standpoint. transformation need not erase the practical differences between dream and waking. the story performs philosophical uncertainty rather than replacing it with a doctrine. warring states & classical chinese traditions daodejing, zhuangzi, and the way

museumExhibits.label: Cook Ding: Skill Without Forced Control
museumExhibits.searchText: cook ding: skill without forced control zhuangzi · skill and nourishing life what kind of knowledge becomes possible when trained responsiveness replaces force? practice, perception, timing, resistance, and the danger of romanticizing mastery expertise changes perception, not only speed or muscular control. non-forcing responds to the grain and structure of a situation. mastery still includes caution when the situation becomes difficult. warring states & classical chinese traditions daodejing, zhuangzi, and the way

museumExhibits.label: Later Mohist Canons: Names, Models, and Argument
museumExhibits.searchText: later mohist canons: names, models, and argument mohist texts · names, models, and reasons how can distinctions and models make public reasoning more reliable? definitions, names, comparison, standards, inference, and difficult transmission public standards require careful attention to names, kinds, and relevant similarities. the canons connect reasoning with practical judgment rather than isolating formal symbols. textual damage and compression make interpretation unusually dependent on reconstruction. warring states & classical chinese traditions mohist debate and fa/statecraft currents

museumExhibits.label: Siege Defense and the Ethics of Consequences
museumExhibits.searchText: siege defense and the ethics of consequences mohism · defense, expertise, and benefit can technical expertise oppose aggressive war without becoming morally neutral? fortification, counter-siege knowledge, impartial concern, and political consequence mohist opposition to aggression coexists with practical preparation for defense. expert knowledge acquires ethical meaning through ends, institutions, and consequences. public benefit must include those outside a ruler’s immediate circle. warring states & classical chinese traditions mohist debate and fa/statecraft currents

museumExhibits.label: Hunayn ibn Ishaq: Translation as Scholarly Method
museumExhibits.searchText: hunayn ibn ishaq: translation as scholarly method translation movement · medicine and language how does a translator rebuild a technical argument across languages? manuscript comparison, terminology, revision, medicine, greek, syriac, arabic, and latin afterlives translation is interpretation constrained by texts, concepts, and specialist practice. greek, syriac, arabic, and later latin histories form a chain with revisions and losses. translators and copyists are intellectual agents rather than invisible carriers. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds translation-era falsafa and classification of knowledge

museumExhibits.label: Aristotle in Arabic: Reception, Reconstruction, and New Questions
museumExhibits.searchText: aristotle in arabic: reception, reconstruction, and new questions falsafa · aristotelian reception when does receiving an inherited philosophy become creating a new one? translation, paraphrase, commentary, curriculum, harmonization, criticism, and transformation arabic aristotelianism arrived through layered greek and late antique traditions. false or uncertain attributions could still become philosophically productive. al-kindi, al-farabi, avicenna, averroes, and their critics did not share one unchanged aristotle. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds translation-era falsafa and classification of knowledge

museumExhibits.label: Ishaq ibn Hunayn’s Euclid: Proof in Arabic
museumExhibits.searchText: ishaq ibn hunayn’s euclid: proof in arabic translation movement · mathematical proof what survives when a geometrical proof crosses language, diagram, and manuscript? definitions, diagrams, proof, revision, technical vocabulary, copying, and mathematical practice a proof depends on the coordinated transmission of words and figures. translation can stabilize technical vocabulary while opening new applications. mathematics helped philosophers test what demonstrative certainty might mean. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds translation-era falsafa and classification of knowledge

museumExhibits.label: Avicenna’s Metaphysics: Essence, Existence, and Necessity
museumExhibits.searchText: avicenna’s metaphysics: essence, existence, and necessity avicenna · metaphysics what explains that a thing exists rather than merely what it would be? essence, existence, possibility, necessity, causation, and the necessary existent essence answers what a thing is; existence answers whether it is actual. possible existents require causes when they become actual. the necessary existent is not one contingent member added to the universe. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds avicennian system: being, soul, logic, and science

museumExhibits.label: Avicenna’s Floating Person: Soul and Self-Awareness
museumExhibits.searchText: avicenna’s floating person: soul and self-awareness avicenna · psychology and self-awareness would a person deprived of sensation still affirm that they exist? immediate self-awareness, body, sensation, soul, thought experiment, and interpretive limits self-awareness need not begin with an image of one’s body. the thought experiment distinguishes awareness of self from awareness of bodily parts. its conclusion and metaphysical reach remain interpretively contested. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds avicennian system: being, soul, logic, and science

museumExhibits.label: Avicenna’s Pointers in Commentary: Logic as a Living Argument
museumExhibits.searchText: avicenna’s pointers in commentary: logic as a living argument avicenna · al-ishārāt wa-al-tanbīhāt how does a compressed philosophical text become a centuries-long debate? logic, demonstration, metaphysics, commentary, objections, resolution, and post-avicennian study compression can create a text designed for expert unpacking. commentators defend avicenna while also changing how his problems are framed. logic remains connected to metaphysics, psychology, and the discipline of inquiry. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds avicennian system: being, soul, logic, and science

museumExhibits.label: Avicenna’s Medicines of the Heart: Embodied Emotion
museumExhibits.searchText: avicenna’s medicines of the heart: embodied emotion avicenna · medicine, soul, and emotion how can bodily treatment and the powers of the soul belong to one inquiry? heart, temperament, emotion, faculties, pharmacology, body-soul relation, and medical context emotions are studied through bodily and psychic powers rather than isolated as “merely mental.” therapeutic reasoning connects general causal accounts to individual conditions. historical categories deserve explanation before comparison with modern ones. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds avicennian system: being, soul, logic, and science

museumExhibits.label: Avicenna in Hebrew: The Canon’s Mediterranean Transmission
museumExhibits.searchText: avicenna in hebrew: the canon’s mediterranean transmission avicenna · translation and medical afterlife how does a systematic work change when it enters a new language and scholarly community? arabic source, hebrew translation, medicine, diagrams, jewish scholarship, and mediterranean circulation translation produces new technical vocabularies and reading communities. a medical encyclopedia can circulate differently from its author’s metaphysical works. islamic and jewish philosophical worlds interact without becoming interchangeable. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds avicennian system: being, soul, logic, and science

museumExhibits.label: Al-Ghazali’s Incoherence: Testing the Philosophers
museumExhibits.searchText: al-ghazali’s incoherence: testing the philosophers al-ghazali · tahāfut al-falāsifa which philosophical claims have actually been demonstrated, and which exceed their proof? twenty discussions, causation, eternity, divine knowledge, resurrection, demonstration, and critique the critique targets selected theses and alleged demonstrations. logical competence enables the objections rather than standing outside them. causation, divine knowledge, eternity, and resurrection require different argumentative treatment. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds kalām, critique, and philosophical appropriation

museumExhibits.label: Al-Ghazali’s Revival: Knowledge as Ethical Practice
museumExhibits.searchText: al-ghazali’s revival: knowledge as ethical practice al-ghazali · iḥyāʾ ʿulūm al-dīn what must happen to a knower for knowledge to become wisdom? intention, habit, virtue, worship, social life, self-examination, and spiritual discipline knowledge is evaluated through intention, action, and formation of character. ethics joins outward practice with inward attention. critique of scholars is directed toward misuse of learning, not learning itself. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds kalām, critique, and philosophical appropriation

museumExhibits.label: Al-Ghazali’s Aims of the Philosophers: Understanding Before Critique
museumExhibits.searchText: al-ghazali’s aims of the philosophers: understanding before critique al-ghazali · maqāṣid al-falāsifa why reconstruct a position carefully before challenging it? logic, natural philosophy, metaphysics, exposition, and the ethics of disagreement accurate exposition is a precondition for serious criticism. al-ghazali adopts philosophical tools while contesting selected conclusions. a paired reading of aims and incoherence reveals argument rather than a slogan about faith versus reason. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds kalām, critique, and philosophical appropriation

museumExhibits.label: Al-Ghazali’s Deliverance from Error: Doubt, Authority, and Transformation
museumExhibits.searchText: al-ghazali’s deliverance from error: doubt, authority, and transformation al-ghazali · al-munqidh min al-ḍalāl what kind of certainty can survive a crisis of inherited authority? doubt, disciplines, testimony, philosophical inquiry, sufi practice, and retrospective narration inherited belief can become an object of disciplined examination. al-ghazali distinguishes demonstrative success from the wider formation of a trustworthy life. autobiographical narration constructs an argument as well as reporting experience. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds kalām, critique, and philosophical appropriation

museumExhibits.label: Al-Ghazali’s Foundations of Analogy: Logic Inside Legal Reasoning
museumExhibits.searchText: al-ghazali’s foundations of analogy: logic inside legal reasoning al-ghazali · asās al-qiyās how can a disputed case be related to an established judgment without guessing? terms, causes, comparison, valid extension, legal interpretation, and disciplined limits analogy requires an argued connection, not mere resemblance. logical distinctions can serve legal and theological inquiry without making those practices identical to falsafa. cases, terms, causes, and purposes all affect whether an extension is warranted. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds kalām, critique, and philosophical appropriation

museumExhibits.label: Averroes on Demonstration: Reading the Posterior Analytics
museumExhibits.searchText: averroes on demonstration: reading the posterior analytics averroes · posterior analytics what makes an argument produce knowledge rather than persuasion alone? first principles, causes, necessity, scientific order, commentary, and trained inquiry demonstration aims at explanatory knowledge grounded in appropriate principles. a commentary can transform a problem while claiming fidelity to its source. different disciplines require principles suited to their subject matter. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds al-andalus: philosophy, law, medicine, and commentary

museumExhibits.label: Averroes on Intellect: The Long Commentary on De anima
museumExhibits.searchText: averroes on intellect: the long commentary on de anima averroes · soul and intellect how can thinking be universal while individual human lives remain embodied? soul, imagination, material intellect, shared intelligibles, individuality, and controversy human knowing involves bodily powers as well as intelligible forms. averroes’s account of material intellect generated divergent interpretations. the latin “averroist” controversy is an afterlife, not a complete description of averroes’s own project. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds al-andalus: philosophy, law, medicine, and commentary

museumExhibits.label: Averroes’s Colliget: Medicine and Natural Philosophy
museumExhibits.searchText: averroes’s colliget: medicine and natural philosophy averroes · al-kulliyyāt fī al-ṭibb how does a general science of medicine relate causes to individual treatment? anatomy, physiology, health, disease, general principles, and clinical particularity general principles and particular cases perform different medical work. medicine connects bodily observation with causal accounts of health and disease. averroes’s intellectual identity cannot be confined to commentary on aristotle. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds al-andalus: philosophy, law, medicine, and commentary

museumExhibits.label: Al-Andalus in Practice: Ibn al-Saffar’s Dated Astrolabe
museumExhibits.searchText: al-andalus in practice: ibn al-saffar’s dated astrolabe al-andalus · mathematics and instrument what happens when mathematical models become portable instruments? geometry, observation, calculation, craft, teaching, timekeeping, and regional knowledge an instrument embodies mathematical assumptions and skilled procedures. craft knowledge and theoretical knowledge interact rather than occupy isolated worlds. regional context matters without assigning every surviving object to a famous philosopher. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds al-andalus: philosophy, law, medicine, and commentary

museumExhibits.label: Suhrawardi’s Philosophy of Illumination: Demonstration and Presence
museumExhibits.searchText: suhrawardi’s philosophy of illumination: demonstration and presence suhrawardi · ḥikmat al-ishrāq can rigorous demonstration prepare a knowledge that is also directly present? light, self-awareness, knowledge by presence, hierarchy, demonstration, and visionary disclosure light functions as a language of manifestation rather than a material substance alone. knowledge by presence differs from knowing through a representation or definition. illuminationist practice and demonstrative argument are joined, not merely opposed. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds illumination and post-avicennian safavid continuities

museumExhibits.label: Suhrawardi in the Margins: An Annotated 1220 Illuminationist Manuscript
museumExhibits.searchText: suhrawardi in the margins: an annotated 1220 illuminationist manuscript illuminationism · early reception how quickly can a difficult philosophy become a shared object of commentary? copying, marginalia, correction, disagreement, teaching, and early posthumous reception marginalia records reading as an active philosophical practice. an early copy can still differ from an authorial text. reception begins through correction, teaching, and dispute—not only through later schools. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds illumination and post-avicennian safavid continuities

museumExhibits.label: Mulla Sadra at Kahak: Withdrawal, Study, and a Difficult Biography
museumExhibits.searchText: mulla sadra at kahak: withdrawal, study, and a difficult biography mulla sadra · life and intellectual formation how should a place enter a philosopher’s life story without becoming legend? withdrawal, study, devotion, controversy, memory, architecture, and cautious biography philosophical formation takes place within political, institutional, and devotional pressures. biographical traditions can preserve memory while also shaping exemplary stories. a historic association is evidence of reception and place, not automatic proof of every narrated event. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds illumination and post-avicennian safavid continuities

museumExhibits.label: After Mulla Sadra: Safavid Learning and the Chahar Bagh School
museumExhibits.searchText: after mulla sadra: safavid learning and the chahar bagh school post-avicennian philosophy · institutional continuity how does a philosophical tradition continue when its institutions and curricula change? teaching, commentary, architecture, patronage, later sadrian reception, and historical distance islamic philosophical activity continues well beyond the period often called medieval. institutions shape which texts, methods, and lineages become durable. later sadrian influence is a history of interpretation, not simple repetition of one master. arabic & islamic philosophical worlds illumination and post-avicennian safavid continuities

museumExhibits.label: Zhu Xi’s Four Books with Collected Commentaries
museumExhibits.searchText: zhu xi’s four books with collected commentaries zhu xi · curriculum and commentary how can editing and commentary reorganize an intellectual tradition? analects, mencius, great learning, doctrine of the mean, examination, and interpretation a curriculum is an argument about what should be read first and how the parts belong together. commentary directs attention while leaving later readers room to dispute the inherited interpretation. state adoption increased zhu xi’s reach without making his interpretation uncontested. confucian renewal & east asian continuities song-ming confucian reconstructions

museumExhibits.label: Zhu Xi at White Deer Grotto Academy: Learning Becomes Institution
museumExhibits.searchText: zhu xi at white deer grotto academy: learning becomes institution zhu xi · academy and rules of learning what architecture and routine does a philosophy of cultivation require? teaching, conduct, shared study, ritual, institutional memory, and the regulations of learning cultivation depends on repeated practices and social expectations, not private insight alone. academies joined textual study to teacher–student relationships and local patronage. white deer grotto became a model through later reception rather than remaining unchanged from 1179. confucian renewal & east asian continuities song-ming confucian reconstructions

museumExhibits.label: Wang Yangming’s Letters to Zheng Bangrui: Philosophy in Practice
museumExhibits.searchText: wang yangming’s letters to zheng bangrui: philosophy in practice wang yangming · letters and moral judgment how does a philosophy change when it is taught through counsel and correspondence? writing, administration, friendship, instruction, decision, and the unity of knowledge and action a letter responds to a particular person and situation while advancing a general claim. knowing is morally significant when it changes attention, desire, and action. calligraphy is material evidence of communication, not a transparent picture of an inner doctrine. confucian renewal & east asian continuities song-ming confucian reconstructions

museumExhibits.label: Zhou Dunyi’s Taijitu and the Song–Ming Debate over Pattern and Heart-Mind
museumExhibits.searchText: zhou dunyi’s taijitu and the song–ming debate over pattern and heart-mind song–ming confucian debate · modern diagram how should cosmic order, material process, emotion, and moral awareness be related? supreme polarity, yin–yang, five phases, principle, material force, and the heart-mind the diagram coordinates generative processes rather than picturing a static collection of things. zhu xi’s investigation of pattern includes texts, conduct, relationships, and events—not only external objects. wang’s heart-mind emphasis is a reconstruction within confucian debate, not a rejection of disciplined inquiry. confucian renewal & east asian continuities song-ming confucian reconstructions

museumExhibits.label: Xuanzang’s Translation Legacy: Terms That Built East Asian Schools
museumExhibits.searchText: xuanzang’s translation legacy: terms that built east asian schools buddhist translation · secondary reception how does translated vocabulary become material for new schools and arguments? sanskrit, chinese, commentary, pilgrimage memory, japanese reception, and scholastic classification translation choices stabilize distinctions that later philosophers can adopt or challenge. commentary and classification produce new intellectual settings around a translated text. japanese commemoration is reception evidence, not a portrait made from life. confucian renewal & east asian continuities buddhist translation, daoist institutions, and the three teachings

museumExhibits.label: Daoist Priesthoods: Canon, Ordination, and Ritual Worlds
museumExhibits.searchText: daoist priesthoods: canon, ordination, and ritual worlds daoist communities · ordination and liturgy what disappears when daoism is reduced to two early philosophical books? priesthood, transmitted registers, canon, liturgy, patrons, temples, and ritual cosmology ritual garments locate authority in trained roles and transmitted institutions. daoist canons preserve diverse revelations, liturgies, biographies, commentaries, and technical works. institutional histories interact with buddhism and confucian governance without becoming identical to either. confucian renewal & east asian continuities buddhist translation, daoist institutions, and the three teachings

museumExhibits.label: The Avataṃsaka Sūtra in Korean Hwaeom: Uisang, Wonhyo, and Interpenetration
museumExhibits.searchText: the avataṃsaka sūtra in korean hwaeom: uisang, wonhyo, and interpenetration korean buddhism · hwaeom reconstruction how did a translated scripture become a specifically korean field of interpretation? uisang, wonhyo, doctrinal classification, interpenetration, manuscript art, and institutions interpenetration asks how phenomena can be distinct without being isolated. uisang and wonhyo developed different intellectual and institutional trajectories. manuscript production is part of a text’s philosophical history. confucian renewal & east asian continuities buddhist translation, daoist institutions, and the three teachings

museumExhibits.label: Huineng’s Chan Lineage in Japanese Zen Reception
museumExhibits.searchText: huineng’s chan lineage in japanese zen reception chan / zen · lineage reconstruction how does a lineage story authorize later practice? platform sūtra, sudden awakening, patriarchal memory, painting, institution, and adaptation lineage narratives connect authority to remembered teachers and texts. sudden awakening did not eliminate training, ritual, or institutional discipline. visual reception can reveal what a later community valued in an inherited figure. confucian renewal & east asian continuities buddhist translation, daoist institutions, and the three teachings

museumExhibits.label: The Three Teachings: Chenghua’s Harmony as a Political Claim
museumExhibits.searchText: the three teachings: chenghua’s harmony as a political claim confucian, daoist, buddhist interaction who benefits when distinct teachings are pictured as one harmonious circle? concord, competition, court politics, composite figures, polemic, and unequal authority images of concord can manage rivalry as much as they celebrate agreement. communities borrowed practices and vocabulary while maintaining institutional boundaries. court patronage gave some formulations of harmony more visibility and force than others. confucian renewal & east asian continuities buddhist translation, daoist institutions, and the three teachings

museumExhibits.label: Buddhist Water-and-Land Rituals with Daoist Star Deities
museumExhibits.searchText: buddhist water-and-land rituals with daoist star deities buddhist ritual · daoist star deities what does direct material borrowing reveal that a story of separate traditions conceals? water-and-land ritual, star deities, imperial commission, liturgical adaptation, and porous boundaries borrowing changes meaning by placing an image inside a new ritual sequence. imperial commission links religious adaptation to resources and political authority. porous boundaries do not make buddhist and daoist institutions interchangeable. confucian renewal & east asian continuities buddhist translation, daoist institutions, and the three teachings

museumExhibits.label: Joseon Korea: Yi Hwang, Ki Dae-seung, Yi I, and the Four–Seven Debate
museumExhibits.searchText: joseon korea: yi hwang, ki dae-seung, yi i, and the four–seven debate korean confucian philosophy · emotion and normativity how do principle, vital force, emotion, and moral normativity meet in one response? yi hwang, ki dae-seung, yi i, seong hon, correspondence, academies, and moral psychology the “four beginnings” and “seven emotions” name different inherited classifications of affect. correspondence made disagreement iterative: replies refined positions rather than merely repeating zhu xi. academies such as dosan gave korean scholarship its own institutional geography. confucian renewal & east asian continuities korea, japan, vietnam, and modern continuities

museumExhibits.label: Yi I at Ojukheon: Qi, Statecraft, and Reform
museumExhibits.searchText: yi i at ojukheon: qi, statecraft, and reform yi i / yulgok · korean confucianism how should metaphysical analysis change institutions and public action? vital force, principle, moral psychology, education, defense, reform, and korean statecraft principle is never encountered apart from concrete configurations of vital force. self-cultivation and statecraft belong to one practical field. reform requires diagnosis of institutions, resources, and habits—not metaphysics alone. confucian renewal & east asian continuities korea, japan, vietnam, and modern continuities

museumExhibits.label: Tokugawa Japan: Hayashi Razan and the Institutions of Zhu Xi Learning
museumExhibits.searchText: tokugawa japan: hayashi razan and the institutions of zhu xi learning japanese confucianism · educational institutions how does a philosophical interpretation become a tokugawa educational institution? hayashi razan, bakufu service, ritual, curriculum, yushima, and institutional adaptation adoption changes a teaching by attaching it to new offices and institutions. razan’s political uses of zhu xi learning were contested by other japanese confucians. yushima’s present architecture marks institutional memory after fires and reconstruction. confucian renewal & east asian continuities korea, japan, vietnam, and modern continuities

museumExhibits.label: Itō Jinsai and Ogyū Sorai: Ancient Learning Reopens the Classics
museumExhibits.searchText: itō jinsai and ogyū sorai: ancient learning reopens the classics itō jinsai and ogyū sorai · kogaku can returning to older words overturn an established orthodoxy? analects, mencius, ancient language, rites, music, institutions, and critique of zhu xi learning philology can be philosophical when changing a word changes an account of human life. jinsai emphasizes ordinary relational feeling and conduct in the analects and mencius. sorai treats the way as a humanly instituted order of rites and music rather than a timeless metaphysical pattern. confucian renewal & east asian continuities korea, japan, vietnam, and modern continuities

museumExhibits.label: Vietnamese Confucian Worlds: Chu Văn An and Lê Quý Đôn’s Vân đài loại ngữ
museumExhibits.searchText: vietnamese confucian worlds: chu văn an and lê quý đôn’s vân đài loại ngữ đại việt / vietnam · teaching, remonstrance, and classification how were classical learning, political duty, and local knowledge reconstructed in vietnam? chu văn an, lê quý đôn, hán learning, remonstrance, history, statecraft, and encyclopedic inquiry shared written classical chinese did not erase vietnamese institutions, politics, or authorship. remonstrance ties scholarly integrity to the risks of public office. lê quý đôn’s classificatory work joins textual inheritance to historical and local inquiry. confucian renewal & east asian continuities korea, japan, vietnam, and modern continuities

museumExhibits.label: Modern Reconstructions: Kang Youwei, Xiong Shili, Mou Zongsan, and New Confucianism
museumExhibits.searchText: modern reconstructions: kang youwei, xiong shili, mou zongsan, and new confucianism reform, metaphysics, democracy, and global philosophy how can a tradition survive rupture without pretending that nothing changed? political reform, buddhist engagement, kant, moral autonomy, democracy, diaspora, and present debate modern continuity is an argued reconstruction, not the passive survival of an unchanged essence. buddhist and european philosophical resources become partners and targets in new systems. confucian philosophy continues across present-day east asia, diasporas, and global scholarship. confucian renewal & east asian continuities korea, japan, vietnam, and modern continuities

museumExhibits.label: Saadia Gaon’s Book of Beliefs and Opinions
museumExhibits.searchText: saadia gaon’s book of beliefs and opinions saadia gaon · kitāb al-amānāt wa-l-iʿtiqādāt how can reason and reliable tradition lead toward the same truth? jewish kalām, sensory knowledge, rational principles, inference, tradition, creation, and ethics reason can clarify revealed teaching rather than serving only as its rival. different sources of knowledge require distinct tests and forms of justification. judeo-arabic authorship identifies language and intellectual setting, not muslim identity. jewish philosophy in arabic-speaking & mediterranean worlds jewish kalām, poetry, law, reason, and revelation

museumExhibits.label: Judeo-Arabic Law and Communal Reasoning in the Cairo Geniza
museumExhibits.searchText: judeo-arabic law and communal reasoning in the cairo geniza cairo geniza · documentary context what lived institutions surround a philosophical text? contracts, courts, commerce, family, correspondence, law, arabic, hebrew script, and community legal reasoning is conducted through documents, witnesses, offices, and material procedures. judeo-arabic joins arabic language to hebrew script and jewish communal use. trade and correspondence connected communities across political and linguistic boundaries. jewish philosophy in arabic-speaking & mediterranean worlds jewish kalām, poetry, law, reason, and revelation
